title: fix(build): refuse dist rebuild under a live managed Gateway
body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes #152284. Source builds can replace hashed modules still used by a running managed Gateway. This change refuses a rebuild when an inspected Gateway physically shares the checkout’s output and gives the operator the matching stop/build/start instructions. Separate candidate trees remain buildable. Related: #155309. The shared service-inspection prerequisite [#151608](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/151608) has landed.

## User Impact

Operators get an explicit stop/build/start recovery path before source builds replace serving artifacts. Failed source builds restore prior output; native recovery refuses to mutate a reassigned service.

## Why This Change Was Made

The installed-definition inventory feeds the real build, tsdown, and run-node entrypoints. Private profile and command facts bind each discovered service; public extra-service output retains its existing shape. A pre-build observation does not lock every sibling against starting during compilation, and unavailable inspection does not establish absence. Template coverage follows the canonical current-account or explicit-selector contract; other active instances without an installed instance definition are not enumerated. System LaunchDaemon runtime inspection and Startup-only Windows sibling qualification remain outside this PR’s coverage. Operators must stop every service sharing the output before a manual build. An absent `dist` directory is outside the physical-overlap proof; logical future-path prediction is not provided. If the built CLI is unavailable, use the matching native service controls. Source-runner stop/restart uses the existing build for recovery; apply source changes with the documented stop/build/start sequence.

The unchanged published 2026.9.4 source-update shell reaches a marked candidate build entry. Its selected-service owner stops the admitted Gateway and the existing output transaction restores previous output after a failed build. Recovery restarts only that captured native service, with current authority and unchanged-definition checks. A reassigned service must remain untouched. The old shell still owns its successful custom restart. The current-main carry removes a retired forwarding helper and invokes the same retained recovery object directly; it adds no replacement owner or alias.

An explicit Windows `gateway start` now enables a verified disabled Task before running it. The existing selected-profile reader and native operation lock remain authoritative; launcher, package-entry or persisted-wrapper fingerprints are checked before enabling and starting. Missing optional Enabled metadata retains the prior Run behavior and never grants enable permission. Captured auto-start policy and older serialized handoff fingerprints retain their contracts. Successful enablement is an independent audited mutation, as in canonical LaunchAgent explicit start; a later launch failure can leave the Task enabled. Inspect the same profile before retrying. Lost authority does not permit compensating mutations against a reassigned Task.

Preserves the original contributor commits and @DonnieFi’s contribution. No release publication or operator deployment is included.

## Evidence

Current candidate: `38a9d0b9b407eb5391aea4a91de7ee07ce9a1b2d`, an ordinary merge of reviewed `d44b984c` and fixed canonical main `b0ee9147076b6ef9552b6ffa3d859b4736888dfa`. Final merge admission found three real conflicts; this successor resolves those owners without changing the source-build recovery implementation (`5d584218` SHA-256 prefix).

The build entry retains canonical argument validation and natural process exit while preserving the published-shell adapter. The Windows control import union preserves canonical SQLite-sharing-error stop/restart recovery and the guarded explicit-start behavior. The managed child process owner is now byte-identical to canonical main, including Linux memory containment. An obsolete pre-spawn authority hook and its sole test were removed: its former shell-recovery caller was already replaced by the native service owner, whose actual authority checks and regression cases remain.

Fresh receiving proof passed **456 cases with one existing skip**: 271 build, managed-lifecycle, memory-owner and published-shell cases, plus 185 Windows service start/stop/shutdown/settlement/fallback cases. The full 56-path changed gate passed all selected type graphs, lint, export scans and repository guards. Fresh eight-pass independent P2 review is scoped-clean. These local controlled tests do not constitute a new installed Windows campaign. Canonical Windows lifecycle proof for the incoming stop/restart owner is separately source-bound; no installed restart or whole-package claim is added.

Historical fixed-main receiving proof and reviews remain retained for unchanged inputs. The original 58-path gate and 129 distinct service/Doctor/source-shell cases are not relabeled as this successor's run. Its [exact-head CI 36388428383](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/36388428383) executed merge `fc6e0032` but stopped in preflight: the Node planner selected 167 rows against the canonical 130-row cap, so product tests did not run. An independent same-request control on its exact main parent `ab07fa87` already selected 166 rows and failed the same guard. Both controls retained all 56 changed paths and 46 recorded flags; all 293 observed planner/module/data/dependency/harness inputs matched. The candidate adds five selected targets and one row, so the complete plans are not identical. Both original guard failures and the local planner-only limitation are preserved. The current hosted review completed with no code or security finding. Under the maintainer's explicit pre-existing-CI authority, the maintained administrative route must verify this new head and attempt; the old d44 packet remains historical, and all 34 skipped jobs remain unrun.

Earlier `c2011fea` receiving proof passed **337 cases with 10 existing platform skips**, including build/fence callers, inventory, Doctor and Windows recovery. Those unchanged contracts retain their original proof. Native receipts below remain tied to their explicit source and package identities; no whole-current-package upgrade equivalence is claimed.

- [Native Windows failed-build run 36306125932](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/36306125932) proved the owned case: exit 17 remained visible, complete output/config/launcher hashes were restored, the Task restarted with a new PID, and RPC verified the original authenticated `82ba7ab` build. The child exited 0 and joined in 95.174 seconds. The reassignment case stopped at a fixture-generated unreadable launcher before its intended callback outcome; that original workflow remains failed. The correction uses the canonical service environment and requires both exit 17 and the typed ownership-change refusal, with full foreign snapshots unchanged through joined failure. The corrected [reassignment-only run 36316083800](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/36316083800), tooling `ea1c6cda`, now passes against exact `c2011fea` source and its dependency graph on the authenticated `82ba7ab` baseline. It preserves exit 17, returns the typed ownership-change refusal, restores every output tree, and leaves the complete foreign Task/launcher snapshot unchanged before and after child settlement. Its source child joined in 73.642 seconds; all four commands joined, four owned roots retired, and final cleanup passed. Both native archives were independently authenticated. The full three-cell reducer remains failed because the unrelated cells were deliberately skipped.
- [Packaged explicit start 36311513816](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/36311513816), tooling `49903aa2` and package `2b0c929c`, passed the real disabled-Task public start in 36.209 seconds. Exact RPC identity, Enabled/running state, unchanged config/CMD/VBS/XML apart from Enabled, seven joined commands, cleanup and retirement were verified. The explicit-false branch matches this source; optional-metadata behavior is separately covered. This is not an identical current-head package or published-upgrade claim.
- [Independent native Task authority 36287470943](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/36287470943) passed owned control, current-foreign refusal, retained-owned-to-foreign refusal and changed-definition refusal with unchanged snapshots, joined commands and cleanup. Its source and package identities are preserved; it is not an installed-updater final-I/O claim.

At the earlier `c2011fea` checkpoint, the API migration was only a direct call to the same retained `restore(true, guard)` operation. At that checkpoint, native restart, revalidation, Task recovery and custody owners were unchanged; the later stop/restart integration is qualified separately above. Canonical main also updates fs-safe 0.20→0.21: the inspected lock/regular-file JavaScript closures are identical, but the Windows addon version differs, so no binary or whole-package equivalence is claimed. The corrected native reassignment proof uses the current dependency graph; the historical owned result retains its original identity.

The later canonical state-owner cutover [#157413](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/157413) is separately qualified at actual CI merge `2e61ea22`. The source-build adapter, retained Task recovery, selected-service revalidation and native operation lock remain unchanged. The stop fallback can acquire the new state owner after `/End` retires the original PID; old native receipts alone do not prove that changed branch. All **77 current-owner cases** passed for state ownership, runtime-publication rollback and drainage, and Task fallback custody on the exact merged source. Its real Windows CI also passed launcher refusal/termination and migrated-update handoff cases. These results support the current dependency integration without claiming an identical whole-package upgrade campaign.

## Published-driver Limits

[Package Acceptance 36263257412](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/36263257412) passed for frozen `82ba7ab`, with authenticated artifact 10913740491. Its [installed Windows campaign 36265838745](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/36265838745) passed fresh installation/discovery/strict preview and cleanup, then the published 9.3 command failed its unchanged 360-second bound despite a successful candidate report and healthy post-timeout RPC. No late observation qualifies that command. The [bounded in-flow diagnostic 36285338074](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/36285338074) linked the old updater’s observed module path to the matching addon retained in its package backup; a separate controlled loaded-addon test demonstrated the deletion mechanism. No in-flow syscall/stack or candidate backup authority is inferred.

The candidate already includes [#154219](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/154219), which removes recursive cleanup retry amplification. The immutable published parent retains its old cleanup closure and omits that transaction from the candidate handoff. Published 9.4 also remains failed. Its separate operator-recovery diagnostic proved `update repair` succeeded without changing the authenticated candidate prefix, then exposed the disabled-Task start issue corrected above. The old callback explanation is source-supported, not a captured primary exception; newer canonical worker cleanup differs, so no whole-worker parity is asserted.

All original red campaign results remain red, with their cleanup outcomes and source identities. No timeout increase, weakened assertion, new controller, schema, or parent-owned backup mutation is introduced. The changed native recovery cases are qualified under the source boundaries above.

[Prior CI 36314559627](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/36314559627) failed a newly inherited main SQLite integrity fixture, repaired canonically by [#159643](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/159643). [CI 36319643888](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/36319643888) then exposed two newer-main SQL-observer test callers and a separate migration-receipt case. Their fixes are now canonical as `e9af8ebc` and `e52420e1` respectively. The latter checks the cached worker's original admission and joins fixture cleanup before deleting state roots.

[Refresh 36329275615](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/36329275615) was canceled without qualification. Its recorded checkout remained the old merge and repeated the old type errors despite a newer PR merge projection. The canonical Codex readback repair [#159735](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/159735) has now landed as `77847b56` and is included in the fixed-main composition. [Historical CI 36338139467](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/36338139467) verified checkout `1872b062`, containing the new head and all preceding fixes, including `1664e4cf`. It exposed additional canonical Tasks/TaskFlow-retirement type and lint leftovers, plus five Codex cancellation/activation regressions. The reported files are byte-identical to its main parent. Canonical [#159836](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/159836), [#159813](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/159813), and [#159841](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/159841) now repair the exact type/lint and cancellation failures; their commits `0b6f02fa`, `ff3c3cbb`, and `ad76f83e` are included in the fixed checkpoint. The unrelated final diagnostics/artifact-selector cleanup [#159819](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/159819) has also landed. [Historical CI 36349123897](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/36349123897) verified actual checkout `dd27aebf`, containing the head and all eight recorded canonical remedies, with all 58 feature files unchanged. It finished with 83 successful jobs, 21 skips, 75 cancellations and two substantive failures plus the aggregate gate: a newly unregistered prior-CI verifier entry, already repaired canonically by `0d02ab7a`, and four orphan-restart integration cases expecting running but observing interrupted. The exact failing test and inspected helper/metrics files match its canonical main parent; the retained original-order log was routed to that owner. The separate PR-context heading check passed after aligning the body with the current template. No retired runtime is restored, no assertion is weakened, and no canceled or failed run counts as passing. The orphan-restart assertion is now corrected canonically by `b459eb600f238d38f8b7156675e5868751f52c54`, preserving the exact interrupted/running table expectations and all other lifecycle assertions. Both it and the Knip entry fix are verified ancestors of captured main `da2bcd69`. Duplicate [#159893](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/159893) was closed without merging; its canceled CI is not passing evidence. [Historical d44 CI 36352027252](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/36352027252) verified checkout `531e0da1`, with parents `da2bcd69` and prior head `d44b984c`. It contains all ten recorded remedies and all 58 feature files match the candidate. The run finished with 55 successful jobs, 21 skips, 104 cancellations and one substantive failure plus the aggregate gate: the existing Codex completion-contention test observed two timers where it expected zero after a retired-turn receipt. Its entire Codex subtree matches main. The canonical owner reproduced the original failure, then qualified the already-landed fixture-scope correction in [#159864](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/159864), commit `aea667c7`: on reproduced graph `327edb6d` and its original Memory-to-Codex order, changing only that fixture yields 242 Memory cases and all 279 Codex cases passing with the zero-timer assertion unchanged. The exact patch and both retained logs were independently verified. This proves the fixture isolation correction, not individual timer callback identities. The maintainer explicitly authorized administrative landing for independently proven pre-existing CI failures. The failed CI run remains failed; branch-specific correctness, security, enforced reviews, source identity and native outcome checks remain required. The maintained exception route qualified that exact old-head evidence, but final live mergeability then found the three conflicts resolved by this successor. No merge request was sent. Current-head checks and review remain required; the old failed attempt cannot certify the changed head.
